questions.question: What is the recommended way to get the RootState type in a Redux Toolkit app with a single store?
options: Write an interface by hand listing every slice's state
Import the RootState type exported by @reduxjs/toolkit
Infer it with ReturnType<AppStore["getState"]> where AppStore = typeof store
Use the any type, because Redux state cannot be typed
questions.explanation: Inferring RootState from the store keeps it in sync automatically: adding a slice to the reducer map updates the type with no manual edits.

questions.question: Why should components use a typed AppDispatch instead of the plain Dispatch type?
options: AppDispatch includes the middleware's dispatch extensions, so dispatching a thunk type-checks
Plain Dispatch is deprecated in Redux 5 and throws at runtime
Plain Dispatch cannot dispatch actions created by createSlice
questions.explanation: configureStore adds the thunk middleware, so the store's dispatch accepts thunk functions. The plain Dispatch type only accepts action objects, so dispatching a thunk fails to compile.

questions.question: Which line creates a pre-typed selector hook in React-Redux 9?
questions.explanation: React-Redux 9 adds .withTypes() to useSelector, useDispatch and useStore. It returns a hook whose state parameter is already typed.

questions.question: A slice file imports RootState from store.ts, and store.ts imports the slice. Why is this not a problem?
options: Redux Toolkit resolves circular imports at runtime
The slice uses `import type`, which is erased at compile time, so there is no runtime cycle
TypeScript forbids circular imports, so this code never compiles
Bundlers automatically duplicate the store module
questions.explanation: A type-only import exists only for the type checker and disappears from the emitted JavaScript, so the runtime module graph has no cycle.
